reference.label: Transmit laser failure
reference.definition: Hardware failure of an optical transmitter laser that removes or invalidates its launched channel.
reference.example: A transponder laser stops emitting, and the remote receiver loses that wavelength.

reference.label: Card failure
reference.definition: Failure of an entire equipment card that removes its traffic or signal and may silence monitoring.
reference.example: A line card loses power, stops carrying traffic, and ceases reporting telemetry.

reference.label: Receiver degradation
reference.definition: Deterioration confined to one optical receiver that creates errors despite a healthy shared optical path.
reference.example: One receiver reports errors while neighboring channels and path measurements remain normal.

reference.label: Laser ageing
reference.definition: Progressive wear of a transmit laser that requires increasing bias current and may culminate in failure.
reference.example: Laser bias rises from 100% to 123% of its beginning-of-life value.

reference.label: Channel margin erosion
reference.definition: Gradual reduction of an optical channel's operating headroom, commonly from accumulated component ageing.
reference.example: A channel's estimated margin declines from 4 dB to 1.5 dB over several months.

reference.label: Fibre break
reference.definition: A physical discontinuity in fibre that prevents light from traversing the affected span or path.
reference.example: Construction work severs a span and downstream receivers see no light.

reference.label: Amplifier output failure
reference.definition: Complete failure of an optical amplifier or its pump that leaves the amplifier with no usable output.
reference.example: An inline amplifier goes dark and all wavelengths through it are lost.

reference.label: Disconnected optical jumper
reference.definition: An unplugged optical patch lead that opens a channel or multiplex-section light path.
reference.example: A patch cord feeding a preamplifier is unplugged, removing its input light.

reference.label: Blocked ROADM port
reference.definition: A ROADM port state or fault that prevents an intended channel from entering or traversing the node.
reference.example: A blocked add port prevents one wavelength from reaching its destination.

reference.label: WSS input-port failure
reference.definition: Failure of one WSS ingress port that blocks every channel arriving on its associated ROADM degree.
reference.example: The west-degree WSS input fails while traffic from other degrees continues normally.

reference.label: Increased fibre loss
reference.definition: Excess attenuation on a fibre path that reduces received power and channel margin.
reference.example: A damaged splice adds 8 dB of loss and drives the channel into signal degrade.

reference.label: Amplifier noise degradation
reference.definition: Increased amplifier noise that lowers downstream OSNR even when output power remains normal.
reference.example: An ageing amplifier maintains output power but adds ASE noise to every channel.

reference.label: Differential group delay increase
reference.definition: An increase in polarization-mode delay that exceeds or approaches coherent-receiver tolerance.
reference.example: DGD rises to 35 ps and causes intermittent OTU framing errors.

reference.label: WSS passband misalignment
reference.definition: Shift or narrowing of a WSS filter relative to a carrier, degrading quality without necessarily changing measured power.
reference.example: A filter shifts 8 GHz off centre and raises pre-FEC BER at normal channel power.

reference.label: Fast polarization transient
reference.definition: A state-of-polarization transition faster than the coherent receiver can track.
reference.example: A fibre disturbance rotates polarization abruptly and briefly disrupts framing.

reference.label: Contaminated optical connector
reference.definition: Connector contamination that introduces attenuation or reflection into an optical path.
reference.example: Dust on an LC connector raises pre-FEC errors until the connector is cleaned.

reference.label: Unspecified failure
reference.definition: A generic placeholder for an underlying failure whose precise component or mechanism is unknown.
reference.example: A remote backward-defect alarm is correlated to an unspecified far-end failure.

reference.label: Amplifier gain loss
reference.definition: Failure to deliver target amplifier gain, producing low output and reduced downstream OSNR across carried channels.
reference.example: An amplifier supplies 12 dB instead of its 18 dB target.

reference.label: Pump ageing
reference.definition: Progressive pump-laser wear requiring increasing drive current to maintain amplifier gain.
reference.example: Pump current climbs to 121% of its beginning-of-life value before an end-of-life alarm.

reference.label: Amplifier gain tilt
reference.definition: A non-flat amplifier gain profile that selectively weakens wavelengths near one spectral edge.
reference.example: Long-wavelength edge channels leave an amplifier 3 dB below central channels.

reference.label: Upstream amplifier failure
reference.definition: Failure of the immediately preceding amplifier, leaving the next optical unit without input light.
reference.example: The previous inline amplifier goes dark and the following amplifier reports input loss.

reference.label: OTN switch-fabric failure
reference.definition: Failure of an OTN cross-connect fabric that interrupts ODUs traversing the switch.
reference.example: A fabric ASIC fails and all ODUs through the switch are interrupted.

reference.label: Wrong ODU cross-connection
reference.definition: An erroneous OTN cross-connect that delivers an ODU to an unintended endpoint without an optical-layer defect.
reference.example: An ODU intended for port 4 is connected to port 7 and produces a trace mismatch.

reference.label: Client-port failure
reference.definition: Hardware failure of a client-facing port or its optic that takes the attached service down.
reference.example: A 100GE pluggable fails and its client service becomes unavailable.

reference.label: WSS attenuation drift
reference.definition: Gradual increase or deviation in per-channel WSS attenuation that leaves the channel underpowered after the node.
reference.example: A WSS setting drifts from 2 dB to 5 dB and the routed channel falls by 3 dB.

reference.label: Card failed state
reference.definition: The observed condition that an equipment card or unit is internally nonfunctional.
reference.example: A shelf reports a line card failed after its processor stops responding.

reference.label: No optical light
reference.definition: Absence of detectable optical power at the observed interface.
reference.example: The input detector reads below its floor after the fibre is unplugged.

reference.label: Digital loss of signal
reference.definition: A receiver defect indicating that no usable digital signal stream can be detected.
reference.example: The receiver asserts dLOS when incoming symbols disappear.

reference.label: Loss of OTU frame alignment
reference.definition: Inability of an OTN receiver to acquire or maintain OTU framing.
reference.example: Severe channel noise prevents the receiver from locating OTU frame boundaries.

reference.label: Equipment defect indication
reference.definition: An asserted equipment-level defect indicating an internal unit or hardware problem.
reference.example: A failed card processor causes the unit to declare dEQ.

reference.label: Traffic alarms masked
reference.definition: Suppression of subordinate traffic alarms while a dominant equipment alarm identifies the failed resource.
reference.example: OTU alarms are hidden while the card-failure alarm remains active.

reference.label: Impaired signal with light present
reference.definition: Presence of optical signal with degraded power, OSNR, dispersion, filtering, receiver performance, or margin.
reference.example: A channel remains present but has low OSNR and increasing pre-FEC errors.

reference.label: Pre-FEC errors
reference.definition: Receiver errors observed before forward-error correction is applied.
reference.example: The receiver measures pre-FEC BER while post-FEC traffic still passes.

reference.label: Signal-degrade threshold exceeded
reference.definition: A received error metric above the configured degradation criterion but short of complete framing loss.
reference.example: Pre-FEC BER exceeds its threshold and the receiver declares signal degrade.

reference.label: OTU frame loss with light present
reference.definition: Loss of OTU alignment despite detectable optical power, distinguishing severe impairment from optical absence.
reference.example: The receiver measures −8 dBm but cannot frame the noisy OTU signal.

reference.label: Polarization tracking exceeded
reference.definition: Polarization variation faster than the coherent receiver's tracking capability.
reference.example: Rapid SOP rotation exceeds DSP tracking and causes a burst of errors.
synonyms: fast SOP change beyond tracking speed

reference.label: Errored seconds
reference.definition: One-second intervals containing one or more monitored transmission errors.
reference.example: A polarization transient produces five errored seconds.

reference.label: ODU-AIS insertion
reference.definition: Insertion of ODU alarm indication signal downstream as a consequence of an upstream defect.
reference.example: After OTU frame loss, the receiver inserts ODU-AIS into every contained ODU.

reference.label: Backward defect indication sent
reference.definition: Transmission of a backward defect indication toward the remote transmitter after a receive-side defect.
reference.example: A receiver that loses framing returns OTU-BDI to the source terminal.

reference.label: Optical channel loss
reference.definition: Absence of a specific transmitted optical channel at the corresponding receiver.
reference.example: A failed transmitter causes the far-end receiver to lose its wavelength.

reference.label: Received traffic loss
reference.definition: Disappearance of payload traffic that should be delivered by a receiving card or interface.
reference.example: A failed receive card stops delivering incoming client traffic.

reference.label: Monitoring silence
reference.definition: Cessation of telemetry, counters, or supervision output from a failed resource.
reference.example: After a card crashes, its performance counters stop updating.

reference.label: Receiver-local errors
reference.definition: Transmission errors confined to one receiver rather than shared by the optical path or other channels.
reference.example: One receiver logs errors while another receiver on the same path remains normal.

reference.label: Normal unaffected operation
reference.definition: Continued expected operation of resources or channels outside the affected scope.
reference.example: Other ROADM degrees continue carrying traffic after one ingress port fails.

reference.label: Rising laser-bias current
reference.definition: An upward trend in transmitter laser-bias current as the laser requires more drive to maintain output.
reference.example: Laser bias rises steadily from 100% to 118% over several months.

reference.label: High laser-bias threshold
reference.definition: Transmit-laser bias current exceeding 120% of its beginning-of-life reference.
reference.example: A transmitter reaches 123% laser bias and raises an ageing warning.
synonyms: LBC above 120% of beginning of life

reference.label: Constant-gain amplifier operation
reference.definition: Amplifier operation that regulates pump drive to maintain a configured optical gain.
reference.example: An amplifier adjusts pump current to hold 18 dB gain as input power varies.

reference.label: Reduced amplifier input
reference.definition: A decrease in aggregate optical power arriving at an amplifier input.
reference.example: Added span loss lowers amplifier input power by 3 dB.

reference.label: Reduced amplifier output
reference.definition: Composite amplifier output below its expected or provisioned level.
reference.example: Insufficient gain leaves all output wavelengths 4 dB below target.

reference.label: No amplifier output
reference.definition: Complete absence of composite optical light at an amplifier output.
reference.example: Input light is present, but a failed pump leaves the output dark.

reference.label: All carried channels lost
reference.definition: Simultaneous loss of every wavelength traversing an affected common optical element.
reference.example: An inline-amplifier outage removes all 80 downstream channels.

reference.label: Multi-channel OSNR degradation
reference.definition: Simultaneous reduction of optical signal-to-noise ratio across all affected channels.
reference.example: A noisy amplifier lowers OSNR by 2 dB across the WDM band.

reference.label: Normal output power with quality degradation
reference.definition: Expected optical output power despite degradation of another quality measure such as OSNR.
reference.example: Amplifier output remains +20 dBm while excess noise lowers channel OSNR.

reference.label: Rising pump drive current
reference.definition: Increasing amplifier pump current used to compensate for pump ageing and preserve gain.
reference.example: Pump current rises from 100% to 116% while delivered gain remains stable.
synonyms: drive current raised to hold gain

reference.label: Pump end-of-life threshold
reference.definition: Pump drive current exceeding the configured end-of-life threshold, commonly 120% of its initial value.
reference.example: Pump current reaches 123% and triggers an end-of-life alarm.
synonyms: pump current above 120% of beginning of life

reference.label: Band-edge channels weak
reference.definition: Lower power on a subset of wavelengths near one spectral edge, characteristic of gain tilt.
reference.example: The longest-wavelength channels arrive 3 dB below central channels.
synonyms: channels low at one band edge

reference.label: OSC not received
reference.definition: Failure of a site or optical unit to receive the incoming optical supervisory channel.
reference.example: An amplifier site reports no incoming OSC after a span fault.

reference.label: Amplifier input loss
reference.definition: Absence of composite optical input light at an amplifier's input monitor.
reference.example: A cut feeding span makes the inline amplifier input detector read no light.

reference.label: Input present, output absent
reference.definition: Amplifier failure signature in which optical input is detected but no output is produced.
reference.example: The input monitor reads −5 dBm while the output remains below detection.

reference.label: Amplifier gain out of range
reference.definition: Measured amplifier gain differing from its configured target by more than the allowed tolerance.
reference.example: A 20 dB gain target measures 17.5 dB.
synonyms: gain more than 2 dB from target

reference.label: Per-channel power re-leveling
reference.definition: Node adjustment that restores a weakened incoming channel to its configured output power.
reference.example: A ROADM reduces attenuation and restores a channel arriving 4 dB low.

reference.label: Residual OSNR penalty after leveling
reference.definition: Persistence of signal-to-noise degradation after a node has restored optical power.
reference.example: Output power returns to target, but channel OSNR remains 3 dB below baseline.

reference.label: Uncompensated low channel power
reference.definition: Below-target channel power propagated because input loss exceeds the node's leveling range.
reference.example: A 14 dB upstream loss exceeds correction range and the channel exits 8 dB low.

reference.label: Impairment passes through node
reference.definition: Persistence of an incoming impairment through an optical node onto the channels routed onward.
reference.example: Poor OSNR on an ingress line remains on each wavelength after ROADM switching.

reference.label: Normal channel power
reference.definition: Per-channel optical power within its expected range despite a possible non-power impairment.
reference.example: A passband-impaired channel remains at −3 dBm while its error rate rises.

reference.label: Reduced channel quality
reference.definition: Degraded recoverability or error performance of a channel while some signal remains present.
reference.example: Passband clipping raises pre-FEC BER without removing the channel.

reference.label: ROADM degree blocked
reference.definition: Prevention of all wavelengths arriving on one ROADM degree from passing through the failed ingress.
reference.example: Every west-arriving wavelength is blocked by the failed west WSS input.

reference.label: ODU-AIS present
reference.definition: Presence or reception of the ODU-layer alarm indication signal representing an upstream defect.
reference.example: A client port receives ODU-AIS after an upstream OTU failure.

reference.label: ODU-AIS forwarding
reference.definition: Propagation of ODU-AIS through an OTN switch on affected cross-connected ODUs.
reference.example: The switch forwards AIS on every ODU affected by the upstream defect.

reference.label: Misdirected ODU
reference.definition: An ODU delivered from an unexpected source or to an unintended endpoint.
reference.example: A client port receives another service's ODU and detects a trace mismatch.

reference.label: Client service down
reference.definition: Loss of usable customer-facing connectivity on the affected client service.
reference.example: Reception of ODU-AIS takes the associated 100GE service down.

reference.label: Defect-free protection path available
reference.definition: Availability of at least one protection member path without a relevant defect.
reference.example: When the working path fails, the selector chooses the healthy protection path.
synonyms: selector can choose a healthy path

reference.label: Brief protection-switch hit
reference.definition: A short service interruption limited to the time required to change protection paths.
reference.example: Traffic pauses for 30 ms while the selector switches to protection.

reference.label: OTN traffic interruption
reference.definition: Loss of continuity for ODUs traversing a failed OTN switching fabric.
reference.example: A fabric reset interrupts every cross-connected ODU.

reference.label: No optical symptom
reference.definition: Absence of optical power or quality indications for a logical ODU routing defect.
reference.example: Power and OTU framing remain normal despite an ODU being sent to the wrong port.

reference.label: ODU trail-trace mismatch
reference.definition: Mismatch between the received ODU trail trace and the trace provisioned for the expected connection.
reference.example: A port expecting trace CLIENT-B receives CLIENT-A.

reference.label: Protection path selected
reference.definition: State in which a protected service is currently carried over its protection ODU path.
reference.example: After a working-path defect, the receive selector uses the backup route.

reference.label: Protection path unavailable
reference.definition: State in which the configured protection ODU path is defective and unavailable for backup.
reference.example: The standby ODU loses framing and can no longer protect the service.

reference.label: Received optical power
reference.definition: Optical power measured at a receiver input.
reference.example: A coherent receiver reports −9.4 dBm.

reference.label: Per-channel optical power
reference.definition: Optical power measured separately for each wavelength channel.
reference.example: An optical channel monitor reports channel 44 at −3.1 dBm.

reference.label: Optical signal-to-noise ratio
reference.definition: Ratio of optical signal power to optical noise power for a channel.
reference.example: Channel monitoring reports an OSNR of 18.7 dB.

reference.label: Pre-FEC bit error ratio
reference.definition: Received bit-error ratio measured before forward-error correction.
reference.example: A coherent receiver reports pre-FEC BER of 2×10^-4.

reference.label: Differential group delay
reference.definition: Measured delay difference between principal polarization modes of an optical signal.
reference.example: Advanced monitoring reports 22 ps of DGD.

reference.label: Polarization change rate
reference.definition: Measured rate at which the received state of polarization changes.
reference.example: Telemetry records a polarization rate above the receiver's tracking threshold.

reference.label: Laser-bias current
reference.definition: Transmit-laser bias current, commonly normalized to its beginning-of-life value.
reference.example: A transmitter reports laser bias at 117% of beginning of life.

reference.label: Composite input power
reference.definition: Aggregate optical power of all light entering an optical amplifier or unit.
reference.example: An inline amplifier reports total input power of −8 dBm.

reference.label: Composite output power
reference.definition: Aggregate optical power of all light leaving an optical amplifier or unit.
reference.example: A booster reports total output power of +20 dBm.

reference.label: Pump drive current
reference.definition: Amplifier pump-laser drive current, commonly expressed as a percentage of beginning-of-life value.
reference.example: A preamplifier reports pump drive current at 121%.

reference.label: OSC receive status
reference.definition: Status indicating whether the optical supervisory channel is present at an optical-unit input.
reference.example: An amplifier reports OSC presence as false after an upstream fault.

reference.label: Client errored seconds
reference.definition: Count of client-interface seconds containing one or more errors.
reference.example: A client port records 14 errored seconds in a 15-minute interval.

reference.label: Client unavailable seconds
reference.definition: Count of seconds for which a client interface is unavailable.
reference.example: A failed port accumulates 900 unavailable seconds in one interval.

reference.label: Transponder
reference.definition: Terminal equipment that maps a client signal to and from a single optical line channel.
reference.example: A 400G transponder carries one coherent wavelength.

reference.label: Muxponder
reference.definition: Terminal equipment that aggregates multiple client signals onto a higher-rate optical line channel.
reference.example: A muxponder combines four 100GE clients into one 400G wavelength.

reference.label: OTN line card
reference.definition: A card that terminates optical OTN line signals and provides OTU/ODU framing and monitoring.
reference.example: An OTN line card terminates a coherent OTU and exposes its ODUs to a switch.

reference.label: Optical amplifier
reference.definition: An optical gain unit monitored for input, output, gain, noise, pump, and supervisory-channel conditions.
reference.example: An EDFA reports composite powers, gain, and pump current.

reference.label: Booster amplifier
reference.definition: An optical amplifier placed at the transmitting end of a multiplex section to raise launch power.
reference.example: A booster amplifies ROADM output before the outgoing fibre span.

reference.label: Line amplifier
reference.definition: An intermediate optical amplifier that restores WDM power along a multiplex section.
reference.example: An inline amplifier at a hut boosts all channels before the next span.

reference.label: Preamplifier
reference.definition: An amplifier at the receiving end of a multiplex section before reception or ROADM switching.
reference.example: A preamplifier boosts incoming line power immediately before the receive-side ROADM.

reference.label: OTN switch
reference.definition: Equipment that cross-connects ODUs through an internal switching fabric.
reference.example: An OTN switch maps an incoming ODU from a line card to a client port.

reference.label: Client interface port
reference.definition: A client-facing physical interface that terminates an optic and reports service and performance state.
reference.example: A 100GE client port connects a customer router to the OTN system.

reference.label: ROADM
reference.definition: An optical node using wavelength-selective switching to add, drop, and route individual channels.
reference.example: A ROADM routes one wavelength east while dropping another locally.

reference.label: WSS degree module
reference.definition: The wavelength-selective-switch module serving one directional degree of a ROADM.
reference.example: The west-degree WSS processes wavelengths arriving from the west span.

reference.label: OCH_LOS
reference.definition: Alarm indicating that no optical channel light is detected at a line receiver.
reference.example: A fibre cut removes receiver light and raises OCH_LOS.

reference.label: OTU_LOF
reference.definition: Alarm indicating loss of OTU frame alignment while optical light remains present.
reference.example: Severe OSNR degradation causes OTU_LOF despite measurable input power.

reference.label: OTU_SD
reference.definition: Alarm indicating that pre-FEC errors exceed the configured signal-degrade threshold.
reference.example: A dirty connector raises BER above threshold and triggers OTU_SD.

reference.label: OTU_BDI
reference.definition: Alarm showing that the far-end OTU receiver reports a defect on the locally transmitted signal.
reference.example: The local terminal raises OTU_BDI after the remote receiver loses framing.

reference.label: EQPT_TX_FAIL
reference.definition: Equipment alarm reporting a locally detected transmit-laser failure.
reference.example: Missing laser output causes the terminal to raise EQPT_TX_FAIL.

reference.label: EQPT_CARD_FAIL
reference.definition: Equipment alarm reporting an internal hardware failure of an entire card.
reference.example: A failed card power rail raises EQPT_CARD_FAIL.

reference.label: LASER_BIAS_HIGH
reference.definition: Predictive alarm indicating that transmit-laser bias exceeds its ageing threshold.
reference.example: Laser bias at 124% of beginning of life raises LASER_BIAS_HIGH.

reference.label: AMP_INPUT_LOS
reference.definition: Alarm indicating absence of optical light at a line amplifier input.
reference.example: A broken feeding span causes an inline amplifier to raise AMP_INPUT_LOS.

reference.label: OMS_LOS_P
reference.definition: Preamplifier alarm indicating loss of composite multiplex-section light at the receiving input.
reference.example: A disconnected input jumper causes OMS_LOS_P.

reference.label: OSC_LOS
reference.definition: Alarm indicating that an incoming optical supervisory channel is not received.
reference.example: Severe span loss removes the OSC and raises OSC_LOS.

reference.label: AMP_FAIL
reference.definition: Alarm indicating that amplifier input light is present but no output is produced.
reference.example: A failed pump leaves the output dark and raises AMP_FAIL.

reference.label: AMP_GAIN_OOR
reference.definition: Alarm indicating that measured amplifier gain differs from target beyond the allowed tolerance.
reference.example: An amplifier targeted at 20 dB delivers 17 dB and raises AMP_GAIN_OOR.

reference.label: AMP_PUMP_EOL
reference.definition: Alarm indicating that amplifier pump drive current has crossed its end-of-life threshold.
reference.example: Pump current reaches 123% and raises AMP_PUMP_EOL.

reference.label: CLIENT_SF
reference.definition: Client-port alarm indicating that a port, ODU, switch, or other failure prevents valid client service.
reference.example: A client port raises CLIENT_SF after receiving a misdirected ODU.

reference.label: ODU_AIS
reference.definition: Alarm indicating that an ODU alarm indication signal has been received from upstream.
reference.example: An egress client port raises ODU_AIS after an upstream OTU defect.

reference.label: ODU_BDI
reference.definition: Alarm indicating that the remote ODU endpoint reports a downstream defect or received AIS.
reference.example: The local client port raises ODU_BDI after the far end reports incoming AIS.

reference.label: ODU_TIM
reference.definition: Alarm indicating that the received ODU trail trace differs from the expected trace.
reference.example: A port expecting trace B receives trace A and raises ODU_TIM.

reference.label: PROT_ACTIVE
reference.definition: Protection-state indication that service is currently selected from the protection path.
reference.example: After working-path failure, the port reports PROT_ACTIVE.

reference.label: PROT_UNAVAIL
reference.definition: Alarm indicating that the configured protection path is defective or unavailable.
reference.example: Loss of framing on the backup ODU raises PROT_UNAVAIL.

reference.label: EQPT_PORT_FAIL
reference.definition: Equipment alarm indicating internal failure of a client port or its optic.
reference.example: A failed Ethernet PHY raises EQPT_PORT_FAIL.

reference.label: OTN_FABRIC_FAIL
reference.definition: Equipment alarm indicating failure of an OTN switch's cross-connect fabric.
reference.example: A cross-connect ASIC failure raises OTN_FABRIC_FAIL.

reference.label: Single optical channel
reference.definition: Exactly one wavelength channel affected independently of other wavelengths.
reference.example: A passband shift affects only the 193.1 THz channel.

reference.label: All carried channels
reference.definition: Every wavelength traversing the referenced common optical resource or section.
reference.example: An amplifier outage affects all 80 channels it carries.

reference.label: Channels on one ROADM degree
reference.definition: All wavelengths entering a ROADM through one specified directional degree.
reference.example: A west-ingress failure blocks every wavelength arriving from the west.
synonyms: all channels arriving on that degree

reference.label: Receiver-only scope
reference.definition: The particular receiver observing a condition, excluding the shared path and other receivers.
reference.example: Internal receiver noise creates errors only at receiver A.

reference.label: Single ODU
reference.definition: One ODU connection rather than all ODUs traversing a switch.
reference.example: A wrong cross-connect misroutes one ODU while others remain correct.

reference.label: All ODUs through a switch
reference.definition: Every ODU whose configured route traverses the referenced OTN switch fabric.
reference.example: A fabric failure interrupts all ODUs through the switch.
synonyms: every ODU cross-connected through the switch

reference.label: Client service
reference.definition: The customer-facing service carried through a client port and associated ODU path.
reference.example: A port failure takes the attached 100GE client service down.

reference.label: Far-end endpoint
reference.definition: The endpoint opposite the equipment or interface currently under discussion.
reference.example: The far end reports loss of signal after the local laser fails.

reference.label: Far-end receiver
reference.definition: The optical receiver corresponding to the current endpoint's transmitter.
reference.example: The far-end receiver loses the wavelength when the local laser stops.

reference.label: Far-end transmitter
reference.definition: The remote transmitter that sends the signal toward the current receiver.
reference.example: BDI is returned toward the far-end transmitter after local frame loss.

reference.label: Upstream optical path
reference.definition: The portion of a channel route preceding the current observation point.
reference.example: A dirty connector upstream of the receiver lowers channel margin.

reference.label: Downstream
reference.definition: Resources or observation points later in the signal-flow direction.
reference.example: Amplifier noise degradation is visible at downstream ROADMs.

reference.label: Feeding fibre span
reference.definition: The immediately upstream fibre section delivering light to the current unit.
reference.example: A cut in the feeding span removes light at the amplifier input.

reference.label: Working ODU path
reference.definition: The primary route normally selected to carry a protected ODU service.
reference.example: A defect on the working path triggers protection switching.

reference.label: Protection ODU path
reference.definition: The alternate ODU route configured to protect the working path.
reference.example: The selector moves to the protection path when the working route fails.

reference.label: Power monitoring option
reference.definition: Optional entitlement or equipment capability exposing optical-power measurements.
reference.example: Enabling power monitoring exposes amplifier input and output power.

reference.label: Advanced monitoring option
reference.definition: Optional capability exposing coherent quality or pump-health measurements.
reference.example: Advanced monitoring provides OSNR, pre-FEC BER, DGD, and polarization rate.

reference.label: Channel monitoring option
reference.definition: Optional capability providing per-wavelength power and OSNR measurements.
reference.example: A licensed channel monitor reports power for each WDM wavelength.

reference.label: 15-minute performance bins
reference.definition: Storage and reporting of performance counters in fixed 15-minute intervals.
reference.example: Client errored and unavailable seconds are reported for 10:00–10:15.

reference.label: Hard failure
reference.definition: Abrupt, complete functional loss that normally causes immediate signal or service outage.
reference.example: A fibre cut producing instant loss of signal is a hard failure.

reference.label: Degradation
reference.definition: Reduced signal quality or margin while some signal or service remains available.
reference.example: A 2 dB OSNR penalty with traffic still passing is a degradation.

reference.label: Incipient fault
reference.definition: Progressive deterioration observable before functional failure or service impact.
reference.example: Rising pump current over several months is an incipient fault.

reference.label: Post-provisioning fault pattern
reference.definition: A fault tendency occurring mainly immediately after configuration or cross-connect changes.
reference.example: An ODU trace mismatch appears just after a new cross-connect is provisioned.

reference.label: Critical severity
reference.definition: Highest operational priority for severe service or major network impact requiring immediate attention.
reference.example: A fabric failure interrupting all ODUs is classified critical.

reference.label: Major severity
reference.definition: High priority for significant impairment or service loss below critical impact.
reference.example: Loss of one unprotected client service is classified major.

reference.label: Minor severity
reference.definition: Low alarm priority for limited or pre-service-impact conditions.
reference.example: An early pump-ageing warning is classified minor.

reference.label: Not alarmed
reference.definition: State in which a monitored condition does not generate an active alarm.
reference.example: A small current increase within normal limits is recorded but not alarmed.

reference.label: G.798 OTU consequent actions
reference.definition: On OTU frame loss, insert ODU-AIS downstream on every contained ODU and return BDI toward the transmitter.
reference.example: A framing defect sends AIS to mapped clients and BDI back to the source terminal.

reference.label: Span-local OSC regeneration
reference.definition: Each amplifier site terminates the incoming OSC and originates a new OSC on the next span.
reference.example: A hut consumes the west-span OSC and launches a separate OSC eastward.

reference.label: SNCP receive-side protection
reference.definition: Protection using working and protection ODU paths with selection at the receiving client port.
reference.example: The receiver selects a defect-free protection ODU after the working ODU fails.

reference.label: Per-channel ROADM switching
reference.definition: ROADM forwarding in which wavelengths are switched independently, while ingress impairments remain attached to routed channels.
reference.example: Two wavelengths from one ingress are sent to different egresses while both retain the ingress OSNR penalty.
